top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B044) has the clearest attribution of the available proposals: Melitz (2003) is a single originating model that moved trade analysis from the industry to the firm, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple is a separable extension. Its qualitative predictions on selection, exporter premia and reallocation have been tested in firm-level data for over twenty years, and the disputes concern welfare magnitudes, not the mechanism. It is a later, distinct advance on the theory recognised in 2008. The weaknesses are real. Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, and arguably Redding, fall outside a two-name award, and the citation should be worded around the theory of selection and the gains from trade, not the magnitudes. I rank P002 (Autor, Hanson and Katz, B038) second. It is an important, well-tested empirical programme, but its boundary is less stable (Katz versus Dorn; one discovery versus two), the task framework has priority claims outside the ballot, and the persistence of China-shock effects is still debated. I rank no award last because both proposals describe mature, substantial achievements. This ranking rests on attribution, maturity and citation scope, not on supporter counts.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the profile documents no connection to Melitz, Helpman, Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Hassler, Krusell and Boppart in a different department, and my field (political science) is not close to either proposal.
